text:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — multiple GPU health alerts firing across us-west-2 pool (ECC errors + thermal excursions). Alert group: gpu.health.signals. Initial aggregator count: 18 in 5m. Thread created 1795004321
Maya: I'm on it. Seeing pages for 3 different racks. Symptoms: transient ECC spikes and a couple of node drains. Any customer-facing errors yet?
Raj: a couple of customers reported increased latency on /v1/generate and 504s during bursts. Not widespread but visible in a few heavy RL agents.
Cleo: grabbing node list now. `kubectl get nodes -l pool=us-west-2-gpu -o wide` returned 6 nodes in NotReady or Draining states.
DevOps-Bot: Drain jobs started: node/gpu-uw2-07 -> cordon+drain (operator-evict).
Maya: OK prioritize: 1) stop noisy pages, 2) protect serving plane from flapping nodes, 3) mitigate customer impact with fallback models.
Tom: quick check of telemetry — thermal spike coincides with ECC burst on nv4x cards. Fan RPMs jump then GPUs report `uncorrectable_ecc` count increments. Node reboots triggered on 2 nodes.
Cleo: Logs from gpu-monitor: ```
[2026-03-10T21:12:03Z] gpu0 ECC_UNCORRECTABLE +3
[2026-03-10T21:12:04Z] gpu0 temp=95C fan=4200RPM
[2026-03-10T21:12:05Z] kernel: oom_kill_process: killed process 4521 (inference)
```
Raj: Inference processes that hit OOM are small subset — looks like long-context RL episodes pushing sequence lengths. Could be KV cache growth + lower VRAM margin after thermal throttling.
Maya: Immediate mitigation steps I'm applying now: 1) enable fallback model variant (smaller quantized) for routes hitting 90th pct seq length, 2) increase autoscaling buffer for dedicated pool by +20% to shift traffic away from draining nodes, 3) suppress ECC alerting noise to paging channel (still record metrics).
DevOps-Bot: Fallback flag toggled for route /v1/inference/rl -> variant 'quant-8-fallback'. Canary enabled.
Kira-CS: Which customers saw errors? I need to notify CS if SLOs breached.
Raj: Two mid-market customers (acct-A, acct-C) saw transient 504s between 21:12–21:20 UTC. No data exfiltration, only request failures.
Maya: Kira, send an informational note: "We mitigated transient GPU hardware errors impacting a small subset of requests; fallbacks enabled; investigating root cause and reducing noise." Keep it high level.
Kira-CS: Will do.
Cleo: For alerting: current ECC health alert is `sum(ecc_errors{job=gpu_monitor} > 0) by gpu > 1` over 1m. That's noisy during thermal events. Proposal: change to alert on sustained ECC rate normalized per GPU: `increase(ecc_errors[10m]) / gpu_uptime > 0.0005` and move to SEV3 instead of immediate page. Also add a thermal hysteresis rule: only page if temp > 92C for 2 consecutive minutes.
Tom: Agree. Also add cross-signal correlation: don't page ECC if there's a concurrent scheduled maintenance or if a node already draining. We get noise when single node reports a burst during drain.
Maya: Good. Action for now: I'll mute the current ECC -> pager rule for 30 minutes and create a follow-up ticket to implement the new rate-based rule + thermal hysteresis.
PagerBot: Pager suppression applied by Maya for rule gpu-ecc-critical for 30m.
Cleo: Dashboard ask: we need a panel that shows per-node timeline columns: ECC uncorrectable count, temp, fan RPM, VRAM usage, and last drain event — all aligned to request error spikes. This will help triage next time. Requesting chart in infra/gpu-health.
Raj: Also add a derived metric: `effective_vram_margin = vram_total - max(rolling_95th_vram_usage)` per model route so we can correlate routes that push the margin low.
Maya: I'll create the infra ticket: INFRA-2246 - 'GPU health: add composite dashboard + implement ECC rate alert + thermal hysteresis + VRAM-margin metric'. Assign to Cleo and Tom.
Cleo: Will take dashboard. Tom you own alert rule update?
Tom: Yep. I'll draft the new PromQL and post here for review. Draft: ```
# ECC sustained rate per GPU over 10m, normalized by uptime
(sum(increase(ecc_uncorrectable_errors{job="gpu_monitor"}[10m])) by (gpu) / ((time() - gpu_uptime_seconds{job="gpu_monitor"})/3600)) > 0.001
```
Cleo: Might want to divide by total events to avoid noise on long-up GPUs. We can test thresholds in staging.
Maya: Meanwhile, customer impact is limited and fallbacks are working. I'm going to hand this to Raj for the oncall night shift. Raj, please keep an eye on the muted pages and confirm post-mit when we've validated thresholds and dashboards.
Raj: Taking handoff. I'll leave a runbook note under /runbooks/gpu-thermal-ecc with steps we just used.
Kira-CS: Notifying affected accounts with the short summary now.
DevOps-Bot: Node drains complete for gpu-uw2-07 and gpu-uw2-09. New nodes provisioned and joined cluster.
Raj: Initial evidence suggests localized cooling issue in rack 7. We'll coordinate with datacenter ops tomorrow for a physical inspection.
Maya: Post-incident actions (short): 1) implement ECC rate alert + hysteresis (Tom) 2) add composite dashboard (Cleo) 3) run a synthetic workload to validate fallback routing doesn't regress QoE (Maya) 4) update runbook and reduce immediate pager noise for aggregated signals (Raj) 5) datacenter ops inspection (ops). Will create the tasks in our tracker.
Cleo: Also recommend adding a slow-moving alert that raises to SEV2 if ECC rate + thermal persists >30m and node still draining — that indicates hardware replacement.
Raj: Noting: suppressing pager noise should not hide genuine data-plane degradation. We'll keep a kibana stream to monitor real-time errors.
Maya: Thanks team. Handoff complete — Raj is oncall. Reopen if pages resume or customers escalate. :white_check_mark:
Raj: Acknowledged. Closing thread for now; will follow up in infra ticket INFRA-2246 with timelines.
PagerBot: Thread closed by Raj at 1795007850.
